description: Killing parrots crashes your game. Note: I did kill other mobs and it isn t just swinging the sword and i got the same result everytime i killed a parrot. 19w40a: [^crash-2019-10-03_20.30.29-client.txt] Description: Unexpected error java.lang.NullPointerException: Unexpected error at atd.a(SourceFile:407) at axx.f(SourceFile:1234) at dmq.a(SourceFile:363) at das.aE(SourceFile:1234) at das.aG(SourceFile:1517) at das.n(SourceFile:1367) at das.d(SourceFile:907) at das.b(SourceFile:569) at net.minecraft.client.main.Main.main(SourceFile:199)
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Launch Minecraft Java Edition 19w40a.
2. Create a new Creative world with default settings.
3. Summon a parrot using the command: `/summon minecraft:parrot ~ ~ ~`.
4. Attack the parrot.
5. Wait for the game to crash.
6. Observe that a `java.lang.NullPointerException` occurs after attacking the parrot, causing the game to close unexpectedly.
Observed Behavior: When attacking a parrot in Minecraft version 19w40a, the game crashes due to a java.lang.NullPointerException, which occurs specifically when the parrot is killed. This issue has been consistently reproducible, as attempts to kill other mobs do not result in a crash, indicating that the problem is isolated to parrots. The crash report generated provides a stack trace that includes several method calls, highlighting the error's origin within the game's code. The specific line numbers referenced in the stack trace suggest that the issue may be related to how the game processes the death of the parrot. Players have confirmed that every time they attempt to kill a parrot, the game crashes, reinforcing the need for investigation into this particular behavior. The crash report can be found at the specified file location for further analysis.
Expected Behavior: When a player attacks a parrot, the game should execute the attack without any errors or crashes occurring. Instead of resulting in a java.lang.NullPointerException, the expected behavior is for the parrot to take damage as intended, allowing the player to continue playing without interruption. This behavior should be consistent across various gameplay scenarios and not lead to unexpected game crashes.
